doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Born in Savannah; meeting his father at 21; mother's records
summary: Moody was born in Savannah in 1925, met his father only at 21 on the road with Gillespie, and says his love of music came from his mother's Chick Webb, Lunceford and Basie records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay, let's just start from the beginning. You were born in Savannah, Georgia, right?
Tell me a little about your family. About your parents?
My -- I knew my mother, Lida [phonetic sp.], but -- but I didn't meet my father till I was 21 years old.
Worked at -- with Gillespie. I was in -- I was with the band and we came to Indianapolis, nap time.

And this gentleman came up to the bus and asked me if my mother's name was Ruby Moody [phonetic sp.] and if my grandfather's name was James Hamm [phonetic sp.] and my grandmother's name was Maddie Hamm [phonetic sp.], and I told him, "Yeah." Everything was
affirmative and he said, "Well, I'm your father." You know. [indiscernible] I said, "Well, what know, pop?"
You know, 'cause I didn't feel anything when he said he was my father, but, "Well, glad to see you." You know, so that's what that was.

And I thought that he played trumpet. And they tell me that he played with Connie Bradshaw [phonetic sp.] off and on or something. But I thought I got my music -- to like music -- from my father, but I got it from my mother because she the one that had the Chick Webb records, and Jimmie Lunceford, Count Basie, you know, the records of that time because she liked jazz, you know. So I really got my musical likes from my mother, I think. And my mother played piano at -- in the church, so -- because we -- I was born in Savannah, Georgia, but I was raised in Reading, Pennsylvania and Newark.
